author_note: independent reference authored without access to the tool code
reference: Layout scenario corpus on a 40 x 30 m walled plan (metres, y up). Symbol category/shape/colour expectations come from Council Directive 92/58/EEC (Annex I s.4 colours, Annex II 2.1 placement and 3.1-3.5 signboard shapes, Annex IV fire-fighting equipment) and ISO 7010 code names; crossing expectations from HSE workplace-transport guidance; the viewing-distance relation d = z*h from the EN 1838 / ISO 3864-1 pattern with z supplied as an input; orphan/schedule/export/no-text/insufficient-data expectations from spec 14 and spec 00 acceptance criteria. Geometry (segment intersection, end and face-ray distances, route far end) and d = z*h are computed by ref.py (stdlib); 19 randomized cases use seed 20260916. Heuristic parameters (facing check 0.5 m, crossing radius 3 m, escape tolerance 1 m, 0.15 m end exemption) are supplied as inputs, never treated as source values.
reference_citations: Council Directive 92/58/EEC of 24 June 1992 (safety and/or health signs at work), EUR-Lex CELEX 31992L0058, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:31992L0058 - Art. 3(1); Annex I s.4 (safety colours), 2.2 (removal); Annex II 2.1 (placement, line of sight, obstacles), 3.1-3.5 (shapes/colours); Annex IV (fire-fighting equipment); Annex V 2.1 (vehicle traffic routes)
ISO 7010:2019 Graphical symbols - Registered safety signs (code letters E/F/M/P/W and sign names as listed at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_7010; standard itself not read)

HSE, Workplace transport - Separating pedestrians and vehicles, https://www.hse.gov.uk/workplacetransport/separating.htm (crossing points 'suitably marked and signposted'); HSG136 3rd ed. 2014 (title page only)

Viewing distance l = z x h, z = 100 externally / 200 internally illuminated: Glamox application guide (secondary summary of EN 1838 / ISO 3864-1), https://www.glamox.com/en/pbs/application-guide/emergency-lighting/rules-and-regulations/safety-signs/
tools.petrov.re spec 14 (safetysigns) acceptance criteria and spec 00 s0.2, s0.3, s0.5
tolerance: Categorical outcomes, counts and rule presence: exact (they are discrete). viewing_limit_m and required_distance_used_m: relative 1e-9 / 1e-6 - products and a hypot of decimal inputs, so only floating-point rounding separates two correct implementations. Every geometric case is built with a margin of at least 0.01 m (boundaries: 0.49/0.52 m, 2.9/3.1 m, 0.9/1.1 m, 0.10/0.30 m) or 0.3 m (randomized) from any threshold, so no outcome depends on floating-point tie-breaking except the deliberate z*h equality case (100*100/1000 = 10.0 exactly). Round-trip facing angles: abs 1e-9 deg.

Whether z = 100 is right for a given sign: only the relation d = z*h is tested with z supplied; EN 1838 / ISO 3864-1 were not read directly.
Symbol artwork fidelity to ISO 7010:2019 (standard not read; only codes/names).
Defibrillator (E010) name and first-aid classification: not confirmed from a read source, so no unsigned-defibrillator case.
Restricted (non-hazard) zones, assembly point coverage, parallel overlapping routes, multi-point route sight lines: no source or unclear semantics.
PDF print legibility audit and 7-language labels: not a numerical/categorical reference question.
Legacy id migration (r1 -> ISO codes): tool-internal history, no independent reference.
coverage: Spec 14 MVP: symbol library categories (5 mapping cases + no-text), sign->object linking and orphan warning, unsigned objects under a source pack vs observations without one, line-of-sight / obstruction heuristic incl. door openings and boundaries, pedestrian/escape vs vehicle crossings incl. marking radius, marking-vs-prevention wording, insufficient data, schedule<->plan identity, export orientation/ID preservation, bad import.
